finding: resolve_engine_endpoint's restart cannot re-establish the bearer in the very race it targets: ensure_running starts with probe_liveness, which keys off the SAME llm_runtime_instances row that still reads status='running'. If the child is briefly still alive the health probe returns 200 -> Liveness::Running -> ensure_running returns Ok WITHOUT spawning -> the second bearer lookup is still None -> BearerMissingAfterRestart -> still 502. Only the error message changed.
resolution: Oracle: the live reproduction's own log ordering corroborates it — the 502 at 00:03:53.302 precedes 'Process stopped gracefully' at 00:03:53.891, i.e. the child WAS still alive when the bearer was already gone, which is exactly the branch that short-circuits.

finding: The added second ensure_running feeds HealthEvent::Crashed into the per-model flap/backoff state machine for what was a DELIBERATE stop. Repeated in-window sends can trip the 5-crashes/60s flap cap and persist_failed the model, which then refuses every future auto-start until an admin clears it — for a model that never crashed.

queuedForced is cleared only in the queued promise's .finally(), i.e. after the re-run COMPLETES. While the queued re-run is executing, a forced call takes `if (queuedForced) return queuedForced` and is coalesced into a request already issued BEFORE the change it is reacting to — the exact failure the file's own comment says joining must avoid. A residual window of the same defect class.

Same window as above, reached independently from the design angle: the documented contract ('forced + in flight -> run again AFTER it settles') is not what the code does once the queued run has started.

A NON-forced call now returns the shared inFlight promise, so it can REJECT with an unrelated concurrent load's error. Previously the `|| state.loading` guard made that an immediate resolve. createLlmModel awaits exactly this call after a successful POST, so a failing background refresh surfaces as 'Failed to create model' for a model that WAS created.

TEST-8's pre-migration seed uses ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING, but skills has only a PARTIAL unique index (WHERE scope='built_in'). Postgres raises 42P10 and the test panics at seed time, before any assertion runs. This is the SOLE guard on the upgraded-install half of the migration.
resolution: Oracle: reproduced by running the test — 'there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'.

finding: the_prune_does_not_touch_user_scope_skills is HOLLOW: it claims to guard the scope='built_in' predicate, but seeds the name 'io.github.ziee/create-workflow-user-copy' while the migration matches on EXACT equality. Dropping the scope predicate leaves that row unmatched, so the test passes either way — the guard between the DELETE and user-authored content is unprotected.
resolution: Oracle: the test also FAILED on its own terms when run, so it was never green to begin with.

finding: Removing io.github.ziee/effective-prompting from the hub seed leaves the committed index at 29 items / 0 skills, but the UNTOUCHED catalog_v1.rs still asserts SEED_ITEM_COUNT = 30 and counts[skills] == 1. Two pre-existing tests break for a reason unrelated to what they test.

Same removal also breaks two e2e specs that install that exact hub_id (skills/skill-detail-drawer.spec.ts:13, skills/skill-in-chat-real-llm.spec.ts:23) — the only e2e coverage of install-from-hub -> detail drawer -> chat. Neither was updated.

hub_version left at 2.0.0 despite the content change. HubManager::initialize only overwrites a cached seed when seed_ver > cached_ver, so an already-booted install keeps listing (and offering to install) the removed skill indefinitely. This is the SAME 'removing the source does not remove the state on an upgraded install' gap the skills migration exists to close — missed for the hub seed.

The design's INV-5 gate states 'exactly ONE validation pass follows a completed download, asserted on an observable consequence'. No such assertion exists anywhere in the change — TESTS.md claims TEST-13 covers it via the upload path, but no test actually counts the passes. The duplicate-enqueue deletion is pinned by nothing and can be silently reverted.
resolution: Oracle: grep of the diff finds no test asserting an enqueue/processing count.

finding: TEST-10's FORBIDDEN list covers only hub navigation and 'template assistants' — two of the thirteen hidden features. This same change removed WORKFLOW and WEB SEARCH content from two skills, and re-adding any of it (or a scheduler / knowledge-base / literature pointer) leaves the acceptance test green. INV-4 is narrowed to what was built.

The desktop acceptance spec is committed UN-SKIPPED while known to fail (pre-existing harness defect), so the desktop e2e suite is red for an unrelated reason; and INV-2's desktop half is left pinned only by a module-graph assertion that measures no geometry.

Of the three states the design enumerates for INV-5, only the missing-bearer one is exercised. No assertion for a running row on a dead port, and the draining state still returns 503 (a send DOES fail there) with nothing asserting that is intended.
The 'never reloads' guard is an always-true assertion: page.reload() PRESERVES the URL, so expect(page.url().startsWith(baseURL)).toBe(true) is satisfied by exactly the edit it claims to block.
TEST-8 asserts a surviving built-in is still listed without waiting for the boot-time sync_builtin_skills task, unlike TEST-10 in the same file. Racy on a loaded box.
The 'for removed in [...]' loop can never independently fail — the preceding full-set equality already covers it. Reads as coverage it does not provide.

The DELETE removes the rows but nothing removes the extracted SKILL.md directories they pointed at; the row was the only pointer. Every upgraded install keeps three orphaned directories forever, with no prune path (the accumulate-forever shape coding-guidelines §5 forbids). FK-wise the delete itself is safe and correctly scoped, and the 202607220100 prefix sorts correctly.
